GOOD TO KNOW

Nothing changes for a running campaign until you choose to use these. Campaigns keep dialling vertically, answering-machine detection keeps its current settings, and the AI dialler manager is an opt-in plan feature that is off unless an operator or reseller switches it on.

Not yet proven with real customers: horizontal dialling and the AI dialler manager have been tested on staging with the call simulator, not on live traffic.

FOR ADMINISTRATORS

Horizontal dialling: a campaign can work through all of a customer's numbers before moving on, however many they have. Each outcome decides what happens next: try the customer's next number, move on to the next customer, or try again later. Your own outcomes get a choice too, per outcome set, and a horizontal campaign cannot be published until every outcome it offers has one. The numbers are tried primary first; invalid and do-not-call numbers are skipped, and each number keeps its own calling hours and limits. A new report shows attempts by number position.

Answering machines: save your own detection settings as named templates under Campaigns → Answering machines, start from a ready-made one with Duplicate, and choose one in any campaign. Campaigns follow the template, so a change reaches every campaign using it; the page shows which campaigns do. Set a default for new campaigns, per client when you use separate clients. Agentless AI campaigns can now detect machines too: hang up, leave the voicemail message or let the AI agent speak anyway.

FOR SUPERVISORS

Moving agents between queues: the Floor has a Queues view. Drag an agent, or several, from one queue to another (hold Alt or Shift to add them instead), or use Move to… on the card. The move asks which skills the new queue needs and at what level, can take away the skills only the old queue needed, and can last for good, until a time or until the end of the shift, when the agent goes back by themselves. Undo puts it back. Agents stay signed in and a call they are on carries on; they are told on their desk.

AI dialler manager (a plan feature): it watches each calling campaign (abandoned calls, people reached, machines, agents waiting, lists running out, failing routes) and, per campaign, either suggests changes or makes them within the limits you set: pace, answering-machine template, caller ID pool, lead order, retry timing, the next chained list, and moving agents between campaigns for a while. It never pauses a campaign by itself. Every change is in a log with its reason and an Undo, there is a daily summary, and you can ask it in plain words on the Live monitor ("why is Arrears slow?"). Anything it proposes in the chat waits for your Confirm. It needs an AI model set up to explain and to chat; without one it still works with plain reasons.

FOR AGENTS

Dial this next: add a number during a call or in wrap-up and tick Dial this next; it is checked against do-not-call and opt-outs at once and becomes the customer's next call. The customer panel shows their numbers in dialling order, which were tried and what happened.

FOR PLATFORM OPERATORS AND RESELLERS

AI dialler manager is a new opt-in plan feature, off for every organisation until you switch it on in the plan.

Installing: the new index for counting a number's calls today is built alongside normal traffic."}
